description: Hierarchical prompt tree for the geometric-spectral framework in Rust. Adds the helix as a CNF axiom that extends clock arithmetic per digit toward infinity with every rotation. Finite CNF instances remain decidable by Cadical; the infinite helical progression is recovered only in the limit of rotations.
collapse_rule: Concrete finite CNF instances (including those generated from the helix axiom) may be collapsed by Cadical. The infinite helical extension and Flag-6 lift remain analytic and external to SAT.

root.title: Geometric-Spectral Framework in Rust
root.prompt: Implement a modular Rust crate realising the geometric-spectral framework with parameterized Φ, Flag-6 scaffolding, and the helix axiom for extending clock arithmetic per digit to infinity via successive rotations.

children.title: Parameterized Φ
children.prompt: Retain full parameterized Φ_{N,M,K} emission, Cadical integration, and model examination.

children.title: Flag 6 scaffolding
children.prompt: Retain Flag-6 CNF family emitter, residual snapshots, analytic lift hooks, and orchestrator. The helix axiom below supplies an additional generator of successive finite approximations that can feed Flag 6.

children.title: Helix Axiom — Clock Arithmetic Extended to Infinity by Rotation
children.prompt:
Introduce the helix as a first-class CNF axiom schema.

Geometric meaning: a helix advances one unit of ‘height’ (or one digit place) with every full rotation about its axis. Clock arithmetic on a single digit is modular (mod b for base b). The helix lifts this modular clock so that each complete rotation produces a carry into a new, higher digit, thereby generating an unbounded sequence of digits.

CNF realisation: for a finite number of rotations R and a fixed base b (clock size), emit a finite CNF that enforces:
- digit variables D_{r,p} for rotation r = 0..R-1 and place p = 0..P-1,
- modular clock constraints on each digit (clock arithmetic),
- carry / advance constraints that fire exactly once per full rotation and open a new place,
- consistency of the helical lift with the residual-vanishing and zero-realisation clauses of Φ.

In the limit R→∞ the successive carries generate the infinite digit string; inside any finite CNF only finitely many rotations and places appear. The helix axiom therefore supplies a systematic way of extending finite clock arithmetic toward infinity while remaining inside the finitary CNF formalism for each concrete instance.

Generate the Rust modules described in the children.

children.title: HelixParams
children.prompt: Define struct HelixParams { pub rotations: usize, pub base: usize, pub places: usize, pub link_to_phi: bool, ... }. defaults: rotations=4, base=10 (or 2), places=rotations. Builder API required.

children.title: Helix Variable Allocation
children.prompt:
Allocate propositional variables:
- D_{r,p} — digit at rotation r, place p (value 0..base-1 encoded in binary or one-hot),
- C_r — carry / full-rotation flag for rotation r,
- A_p — place-active flag (place p has been opened by a previous carry),
- optional linkage variables that connect the highest active place to residual indices or zero indices of Φ.
Provide dense DIMACS identifiers and a bidirectional map.

children.title: Helix CNF Clauses (Clock + Carry + Advance)
children.prompt:
Emit the following clause groups for any HelixParams:

1. Clock-arithmetic constraints: each digit D_{r,p} satisfies 0 ≤ value < base (one-hot or binary modular constraints).
2. Rotation-advance: after a full rotation the carry C_r becomes true exactly once.
3. Place-opening: when C_r is true a new place A_{p+1} is activated and the digit sequence is extended.
4. Consistency across rotations: digits and carries form a coherent helical trajectory (no contradictory carries, monotonic place activation).
5. Optional Φ-linkage (when link_to_phi = true): the number of active places or the highest digit value is forced to correlate with residual-vanishing or with the number of realised zeros, so that each additional rotation supplies a finer finite approximation usable by Flag 6.

All groups remain finite for finite rotations/places.

children.title: emit_helix and Combined Φ+Helix Instances
children.prompt: Implement emit_helix(params: HelixParams) -> CnfFormula. Also implement emit_phi_with_helix(phi: PhiParams, helix: HelixParams) -> CnfFormula that conjoins the Φ clauses with the helix clauses under the linkage variables. Provide DIMACS export and Cadical solving for the combined instances. Unit tests must verify that small helical clocks (e.g. base=2, rotations=3) are SAT and that successive rotations correctly open new places.

children.title: Documentation of the Helical Extension to Infinity
children.prompt:
Document explicitly:

- Each finite helical CNF instance encodes only finitely many rotations and places.
- The intended infinite object is the limit of the digit string produced by infinitely many rotations (the infinite helical unwind of clock arithmetic).
- This limit lives at the level of set theory / analysis; it is not an object inside any single CNF formula.
- The helix axiom therefore gives a systematic generator of finite approximations that can be fed to Cadical and to the Flag-6 residual-snapshot machinery, but does not by itself close Flag 6 or prove residual vanishing for the genuine continuous spectrum.

The boundary between the finitary helical CNF and the analytic infinite helix must remain visible in the crate documentation.
